name: ScriptaHub – Add books
description: Process a fixed batch of book requests through isolated Create book subflows; record failures separately and continue with the remaining books.

tasks.name: Reserve batch and select first request
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Verify create-book is in the supplied runnable child catalogue before reserving or claiming. Run preflight, then batch-start with {"taskType":"add-book"} once from the flow root. The helper resumes a queued/active batch or replaces a service-confirmed closed/exhausted one. This startup selector has no incoming traversal edge.

If create-book is unavailable, report the catalogue blocker before any reservation/claim. Preserve an existing claim and its durable paths for recovery. For pre-claim preflight/access failure, close the batch when safe, retain the actual error and take batch-to-result.

Run batch-next. Route a returned item, including publicationPending=true, to batch-to-book as exactly one create-book child. Give it taskDirectory, claimedPath when present, executionId, handoffPath and the actual pending-publication flag. The child shares this working directory and resumes accepted artifacts. The run-workflows node returns through book-to-reconcile; continueOnChildFailure=true lets reconciliation handle this item independently. Route task=null to batch-to-result.

For an item, return the runtime's creator fields:
# nextEdgeId
batch-to-book
# afterWorkflowsEdgeId
book-to-reconcile
# workflow
create-book
# prompt
Process this single reserved request using its unchanged identity and durable paths; include the actual item identity, paths and publicationPending value.
# nextNodePrompt
Compact item identity and handoff path.

For an exhausted batch or pre-claim failure, return only nextEdgeId=batch-to-result and nextNodePrompt with the actual outcome.

tasks.name: Select next reserved request
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Verify create-book is in the supplied runnable child catalogue. Continue the saved batch after the preceding item is confirmed terminal or durably deferred. Call only batch-next for selection; keep the existing batch identity and leave later arrivals for the next parent execution. Refresh preflight when its validity expires.

If create-book is unavailable, report the catalogue blocker before any reservation/claim. Preserve an existing claim and its durable paths for recovery. For pre-claim preflight/access failure, close the batch when safe, retain the actual error and take next-to-result.

Run batch-next. Route a returned item, including publicationPending=true, to next-to-book as exactly one create-book child. Give it taskDirectory, claimedPath when present, executionId, handoffPath and the actual pending-publication flag. The child shares this working directory and resumes accepted artifacts. The run-workflows node returns through book-to-reconcile; continueOnChildFailure=true lets reconciliation handle this item independently. Route task=null to next-to-result.

For an item, return the runtime's creator fields:
# nextEdgeId
next-to-book
# afterWorkflowsEdgeId
book-to-reconcile
# workflow
create-book
# prompt
Process this single reserved request using its unchanged identity and durable paths; include the actual item identity, paths and publicationPending value.
# nextNodePrompt
Compact item identity and handoff path.

For an exhausted batch or pre-claim failure, return only nextEdgeId=next-to-result and nextNodePrompt with the actual outcome.

tasks.name: Confirm the book request result
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Handle the single preceding create-book child outcome, including a graph-level failure or termination before any child result existed. Read the most recent creator handoff for taskDirectory/executionId and that item's existing claimed.json/handoff.json. Read only the child state/error and current request evidence, never another book's files. Use scriptahub-tasks status once.

If the service confirms completed, failed or cancelled, retain its actual outcome and take item-to-next. A successful child graph alone is not proof of publication: require the service receipt. If the child failed/terminated while the service still shows running and publicationPending is false, attempt finish state=failed with the child's actual error and retained artifact paths; a stopped task may be acknowledged with finish state=cancelled. Do not fabricate a success or alter output bytes. Finish may refuse while a remote processing job or publication is active: preserve that error as evidence, never weaken its guard.

If publicationPending=true, a remote job is still active, finish cannot safely finalize the item, or the child ended without resolving its running state, use batch-defer with {taskId,executionId,reason:<actual concise cause>} from the parent flow root. This durably skips only this identified item for the current batch and keeps its execution and reservation intact. Never release its processing artifacts, overwrite its package, call claim again or start a duplicate child. Do not poll indefinitely or block unrelated books. After batch-defer succeeds take item-to-next with deferred=true and the exact task identity/reason. The next batch-next call processes other reserved items and closes traversal with active deferred items still reserved. Later batches may process new arrivals without stealing these executions.

An unavailable batch/status service is a shared infrastructure failure, not proof of one task's failure: report that exact blocker without pretending the item was settled or deferred. Return nextNodePrompt with taskDirectory, taskId, executionId, actual outcome (terminal or deferred) and evidence paths. Use nextEdgeId=item-to-next only after terminal confirmation or successful durable deferral.

tasks.name: Summarize publication results
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Read the durable batch through scriptahub-tasks batch-status with {}; this returns the original snapshot without reserving anything, never new arrivals. Report actual completed, failed, cancelled and unprocessed counts and the relative artifact directories. Report deferred items separately with their actual reasons and retained execution IDs. They are neither published nor successful. If traversal is not closed and all remaining active items were explicitly deferred, use batch-close with {retainActive:true}; this releases only unstarted/terminal reservations and preserves active deferred reservations. Never call ordinary batch-close while active work exists. Never overwrite an uncertain publication or claim more work. Report any preflight or service failure precisely. This is the end of the batch; do not loop or start another flow.

defaultObjective: Process the fixed batch of waiting book requests through isolated create-book subflows; retain each actual outcome, skip durably deferred items and continue other books, then report successes, failures and deferred recoveries separately.
